sentences.zh: 璞嘗為人葬，帝微服往觀之，因問主人何以葬龍角，此法當滅族。

translations.literal: Pu once buried someone—Emperor disguised went observe—thereupon asked master why bury dragon horn—this law ought extinguish clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu once directed a burial that Ming Emperor inspected incognito; he challenged the host for burying on dragon horns—a prescription for clan extinction.

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「郭璞雲此葬龍耳，不出三年當致天子也。」

translations.literal: The host said: "Guo Pu said this burial was the dragon's ear; within three years it would bring the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The host said: "Guo Pu said this burial was the dragon's ear; within three years it would bring the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「出天子邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Will it produce a Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Will it produce a Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「能致天子問耳。」

translations.literal: He answered: "It can bring the Son of Heaven to ask, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "It can bring the Son of Heaven to ask, that is all."

sentences.zh: 帝甚異之。

translations.literal: Emperor greatly marvelled him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marvelled.

sentences.zh: 璞素與桓彝友善，彝每造之，或值璞在婦間，便入。

translations.literal: Pu by nature friendly with Huan Yi—Yi each visited him—or happened Pu among wives—then entered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu befriended Huan Yi, who walked in unannounced even when Guo was among his women.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「卿來，他處自可徑前，但不可廁上相尋耳。

translations.literal: Pu said: You come—elsewhere self may go straight forward—but may not on privy mutually seek ear.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu warned: "Elsewhere enter freely—never search me out in the privy.

sentences.zh: 必客主有殃。」

translations.literal: There will surely be disaster for both guest and host."
translations.idiomatic: There will surely be disaster for both guest and host."

sentences.zh: 彝後因醉詣璞，正逢在廁，掩而觀之，見璞裸身被髮，銜刀設醊。

translations.literal: Yi afterward because drunk visited Pu—happened met on privy—screened observed—saw Pu naked body loose hair—bite knife set offering.
translations.idiomatic: Later a drunken Huan Yi peeked into the latrine and saw Guo Pu naked, hair loose, biting a blade before an altar.

sentences.zh: 璞見彝，撫心大驚曰：「吾每屬卿勿來，反更如是！

translations.literal: Pu saw Yi—stroked heart greatly startled said: I always instructed you not come—instead even thus!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu clutched his chest: "I forbade you—and still you came!

sentences.zh: 非但禍吾，卿亦不免矣。

translations.literal: Not only harms me—you also not exempt.
translations.idiomatic: You doom yourself as well as me.

sentences.zh: 天實為之，將以誰咎！」

translations.literal: Heaven truly does this; whom can we blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven truly does this; whom can we blame?"

sentences.zh: 璞終嬰王敦之禍，彝亦死蘇峻之難。

translations.literal: Pu ended suffered Wang Dun calamity—Yi also died Su Jun rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu fell to Wang Dun and Huan Yi died in Su Jun's coup.

sentences.zh: 王敦之謀逆也，溫嶠、庾亮使璞筮之，璞對不決。

translations.literal: Wang Dun's plotting rebellion—Wen Qiao, Yu Liang ordered Pu divine—Pu answered undecided.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun plotted rebellion Wen Qiao and Yu Liang asked Guo Pu to divine; he hedged.

sentences.zh: 嶠、亮復令占己之吉凶，璞曰：「大吉。」

translations.literal: Wen Qiao and Yu Liang again had him divine their own good and bad fortune. Guo Pu said: "Greatly auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao and Yu Liang again had him divine their own good and bad fortune. Guo Pu said: "Greatly auspicious."

sentences.zh: 嶠等退，相謂曰：「璞對不了，是不敢有言，或天奪敦魄。

translations.literal: Qiao etc. withdrew—mutually said: Pu answer undecided—is dare not have speech—or heaven steals Dun soul.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew whispering: "His silence feared frank speech—or heaven seized Wang Dun's wits.

sentences.zh: 今吾等與國家共舉大事，而璞雲大吉，是為舉事必有成也。」

translations.literal: Now we are raising a great undertaking together with the state, and Guo Pu says it is greatly auspicious; this means the undertaking will certainly succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Now we are raising a great undertaking together with the state, and Guo Pu says it is greatly auspicious; this means the undertaking will certainly succeed."

sentences.zh: 於是勸帝討敦。

translations.literal: Thereupon urged Emperor punish Dun.
translations.idiomatic: They urged Ming Emperor to strike Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 初，璞每言「殺我者山宗」，至是果有姓崇者構璞於敦。

translations.literal: At first Pu each said 'Kill me mountain clan'—when arrived indeed someone surname Chong framed Pu before Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu once predicted "Mountain clan will kill me"—a man surnamed Chong—homophone for clan—slandered him to Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 敦將舉兵，又使璞筮。

translations.literal: Dun about raise troops—again ordered Pu divine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun prepared rebellion and ordered another casting.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「無成。」

translations.literal: Pu said: Without success.
translations.idiomatic: "No success," said Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 敦固疑璞之勸嶠、亮，又聞卦凶，乃問璞曰；

translations.literal: Dun firmly suspected Pu's urging Qiao, Liang—again heard hexagram ill—then asked Pu saying:
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious of Guo Pu's loyalty to Wen Qiao and Yu Liang and hearing ill omens Wang Dun demanded:

sentences.zh: 「卿更筮吾壽幾何？」

translations.literal: "You should divine again: how long is my life?"
translations.idiomatic: "You should divine again: how long is my life?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「思向卦，明公起事，必禍不久。

translations.literal: Answered: Thinking toward hexagram—Illustrious Duke raises affair—must calamity not long.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu replied: "Your former hexagram promises swift disaster once you move.

sentences.zh: 若住武昌，壽不可測。」

translations.literal: If you remain in Wuchang, your lifespan cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: If you remain in Wuchang, your lifespan cannot be measured."

sentences.zh: 敦大怒曰：「卿壽幾何？」

translations.literal: Dun greatly angry said: Sir lifespan how much?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun raged: "And your span?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「命盡今日日中。」

translations.literal: He said: "My life ends at noon today."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "My life ends at noon today."

sentences.zh: 敦怒，收璞，詣南岡斬之。

translations.literal: Dun angry—seized Pu—went South Ridge beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun seized Guo Pu and marched him to South Ridge for execution.

sentences.zh: 璞臨出，謂行刑者欲何之。

translations.literal: Pu about exit—asked executioner intend where.
translations.idiomatic: Walking out Guo Pu asked where they headed.

sentences.zh: 曰：「南岡頭。」

translations.literal: He said: "At the head of the southern ridge."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "At the head of the southern ridge."

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「必在雙柏樹下。」

translations.literal: Guo Pu said: "It must be beneath twin cypress trees."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said: "It must be beneath twin cypress trees."

sentences.zh: 既至，果然。

translations.literal: Having arrived—indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: They found exactly that.

sentences.zh: 復云：「此樹應有大鵲巢。」

translations.literal: He also said: "This tree should have a large magpie nest."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "This tree should have a large magpie nest."

sentences.zh: 眾索之不得。

translations.literal: Crowd searched it—not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Searchers found nothing.

sentences.zh: 璞更令尋覓，果於枝間得一大鵲巢，密葉蔽之。

translations.literal: Pu further ordered seek—indeed on branches obtained one great magpie nest—dense leaves concealed it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu pointed higher; they found a huge nest hidden in the canopy.

sentences.zh: 初，璞中興初行經越城，間遇一人，呼其姓名，因以袴褶遺之。

translations.literal: At first Pu Restoration early travelled passed Yue city—between met one man—called his name—thereby with trousers jacket gifted him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Restoration Guo Pu crossed Yue City, hailed a stranger by name, and gave him riding clothes.

sentences.zh: 其人辭不受，璞曰：「但取，後自當知。」

translations.literal: The man declined and would not accept them, but Guo Pu said: "Just take them; later you will naturally understand."
translations.idiomatic: The man declined and would not accept them, but Guo Pu said: "Just take them; later you will naturally understand."

sentences.zh: 其人遂受而去。

translations.literal: That man then accepted and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The stranger accepted and left.

sentences.zh: 至是，果此人行刑。

translations.literal: When arrived—indeed this man carried out execution.
translations.idiomatic: That same man later wielded the headsman's blade.

sentences.zh: 時年四十九。

translations.literal: Age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 及王敦平，追贈弘農太守。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun pacified—posthumously gifted Hongnong Grand Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun fell the court posthumously named him governor of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 初，庾翼幼時嘗令璞筮公家及身，卦成，曰：「建元之末丘山傾，長順之初子凋零。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu Yi was young, he once had Guo Pu divine the fate of the ducal house and himself. When the hexagram was completed, Pu said: "At the end of Jianyuan the hills will topple; at the beginning of Changshun the sons will wither."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yu Yi was young, he once had Guo Pu divine the fate of the ducal house and himself. When the hexagram was completed, Pu said: "At the end of Jianyuan the hills will topple; at the beginning of Changshun the sons will wither."

sentences.zh: 及康帝即位，將改元為建元，或謂庾冰曰：「子忘郭生之言邪？

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended the throne and was about to change the era name to Jianyuan, someone said to Yu Bing: "Have you forgotten Master Guo's words?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Kang ascended the throne and was about to change the era name to Jianyuan, someone said to Yu Bing: "Have you forgotten Master Guo's words?

sentences.zh: 丘山上名，此號不宜用。」

translations.literal: Qiu and shan are the upper parts of the name Jian; this title should not be used."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu and shan are the upper parts of the name Jian; this title should not be used."

sentences.zh: 冰撫心歎恨。

translations.literal: Bing stroked heart sighed regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing smote his breast in regret.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，何充改元為永和，庾翼歎曰：「天道精微，乃當如是。

translations.literal: When the emperor died and He Chong changed the era name to Yonghe, Yu Yi sighed: "The Way of Heaven is so subtle that it is actually like this.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died and He Chong changed the era name to Yonghe, Yu Yi sighed: "The Way of Heaven is so subtle that it is actually like this.

sentences.zh: 長順者，永和也，吾庸得免乎！」

translations.literal: Changshun is Yonghe. How can I escape!"
translations.idiomatic: Changshun is Yonghe. How can I escape!"

sentences.zh: 其年翼卒。

translations.literal: That year Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi died that year.

sentences.zh: 冰又令筮其後嗣，卦成，曰：「卿諸子並當貴盛，然有白龍者，凶徵至矣。

translations.literal: Yu Bing also had him divine his later heirs. When the hexagram was completed, Pu said: "Your sons will all be noble and flourishing, but if there is a white dragon, the ominous sign has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing also had him divine his later heirs. When the hexagram was completed, Pu said: "Your sons will all be noble and flourishing, but if there is a white dragon, the ominous sign has arrived.

sentences.zh: 若墓碑生金，庾氏之大忌也。」

translations.literal: If metal grows on a grave stele, it is the great taboo of the Yu clan."
translations.idiomatic: If metal grows on a grave stele, it is the great taboo of the Yu clan."

sentences.zh: 後冰子蘊為廣州刺史，妾房內忽有一新生白狗子，莫知所由來，其妾秘愛之，不令蘊知。

translations.literal: Later Bing son Yun became Guangzhou prefect—concubine chamber inside suddenly had one newborn white puppy—none knew whence—concubine secretly loved—did not let Yun know.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing's son Yu Yun governed Guangzhou where a concubine secretly raised a newborn white pup.

sentences.zh: 狗轉長大，蘊入，是狗眉眼分明，又身至長而弱，異于常狗，蘊甚怪之。

translations.literal: Dog gradually grew large—Yun entered—this dog eyebrows eyes distinct—again body arrived long yet weak—different from usual dogs—Yun greatly marvelled.
translations.idiomatic: It grew oddly human in face yet weak in limb until Yu Yun noticed.

sentences.zh: 將出，共視在眾人前，忽失所在。

translations.literal: About exit—together viewed before crowd—suddenly lost whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yun drew it before witnesses it vanished.

sentences.zh: 蘊慨然曰：「殆白龍乎！

translations.literal: Yu Yun sighed deeply and said: "Is this not the white dragon?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yun sighed deeply and said: "Is this not the white dragon?

sentences.zh: 庾氏禍至矣。」

translations.literal: The Yu clan's disaster has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan's disaster has arrived."

sentences.zh: 又墓碑生金。

translations.literal: Again tombstone grew metal.
translations.idiomatic: Metal later filmed their tombstones.

sentences.zh: 俄而為桓溫所滅，終如其言。

translations.literal: Shortly by Huan Wen extinguished—ended like his words.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen soon wiped them out as predicted.

sentences.zh: 璞之占驗，皆如此類也。

translations.literal: Pu's divination verification—all like this category.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu's auguries ran true in such cases.

sentences.zh: 璞撰前後筮驗六十餘事，名為《洞林》。

translations.literal: Pu composed front-back divination verification sixty-odd affairs—named Piercing Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu compiled sixty divination cases in Piercing the Forest.

sentences.zh: 又抄京、費諸家要最，更撰《新林》十篇、《卜韻》一篇。

translations.literal: Again excerpted Jing, Fei masters essentials—again composed New Forest ten chapters—Divination Rhymes one chapter.
translations.idiomatic: He excerpted Jing Fang and Fei Zhi and wrote New Forest in ten fascicles plus Rhymes for Divination.

sentences.zh: 注釋《爾雅》，別為《音義》、《圖譜》。

translations.literal: Annotated Erya—separately made Sounds Meanings—Charts Catalogue.
translations.idiomatic: He glossed Erya with separate pronunciations, meanings, and illustrations.

sentences.zh: 又注《三蒼》、《方言》、《穆天子傳》、《山海經》及《楚辭》、《子虛》、《上林賦》數十萬言，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: Again annotated Three Archives—Dialect—Mu Son of Heaven Travels—Mountains Seas Classic—and Chu Lyrics—Sir Vacuity—Upper Woods Fu several hundred thousand characters—all transmitted on age.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the Three Archives, Dialect, Travels of Mu Son of Heaven, Classic of Mountains and Seas, Chu Ci, Sir Vacuity, and Upper Woods Fu—hundreds of thousands of characters still circulating.

sentences.zh: 所作詩賦誄頌亦數萬言。

translations.literal: Composed poems fu elegies eulogies also several tens thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: His poems, fu, elegies, and encomia ran tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 子驁，官至臨賀太守。

translations.literal: Son Ao—office reached Linhe Grand Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo Ao rose to governor of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 葛洪

translations.literal: Ge Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Ge Hong.

sentences.zh: 葛洪，字稚川，丹陽句容人也。

translations.literal: Ge Hong, courtesy Zhichuan—was man of Jurong in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong, courtesy name Zhichuan, came from Jurong in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖系，吳大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Ancestor Xi—Wu era Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Ge Xi served Wu as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 父悌，吳平後入晉，為邵陵太守。

translations.literal: Father Ti—after Wu pacified entered Jin—became Shaoling Grand Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ge Ti entered Jin service after Wu fell and governed Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 洪少好學，家貧，躬自伐薪以貿紙筆，夜輒寫書誦習，遂以儒學知名。

translations.literal: Hong youth loved learning—family poor—personally chopped firewood trade paper brush—night always wrote books recite practice—thereupon by Ru learning known.
translations.idiomatic: Poor yet diligent Ge Hong chopped fuel to buy paper, copying texts by night until scholars noted him.

sentences.zh: 性寡欲，無所愛玩，不知棋局幾道，摴蒱齒名。

translations.literal: Nature few desires—nothing loved play—did not know chess board how many lines—chupu tooth names.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked worldly cravings—never learned chess lines or dice names.

sentences.zh: 為人木訥，不好榮利，閉門卻掃，未嘗交遊。

translations.literal: As person wooden clumsy—did not love glory profit—closed gate swept courtyard—never travelled socialize.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn and uninterested in fame he barred his gate and seldom socialized.

sentences.zh: 于余杭山見何幼道、郭文舉，目擊而已，各無所言。

translations.literal: At Yuhang mountain saw He Youdao, Guo Wenju—eye witnessed only—each without speech.
translations.idiomatic: On Yuhang Mountain he met He Youdao and Guo Wenju—they exchanged only glances.

sentences.zh: 時或尋書問義，不遠數千里崎嶇冒涉，期於必得，遂究覽典籍，尤好神仙導養之法。

translations.literal: Sometimes sought books asked meanings—not far several thousand li rugged risk ford—deadline must obtain—thereupon thoroughly perused canons—especially loved transcendents guiding nourishment arts.
translations.idiomatic: At times, when searching for books and asking about their meaning, he did not shrink from rough journeys of several thousand li, determined to obtain what he sought; he then mastered the classics and especially loved methods of immortality, breathing, and self-nourishment.

sentences.zh: 從祖玄，吳時學道得仙，號曰葛仙公，以其練丹秘術授弟子鄭隱。

translations.literal: Granduncle Xuan—Wu time studied Dao attained transcendence—styled Ge Immortal Duke—with his cinnabar refining secret arts taught disciple Zheng Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His granduncle Ge Xuan became famed Ge Immortal Duke and passed cinnabar secrets to Zheng Yin.

sentences.zh: 洪就隱學，悉得其法焉。

translations.literal: Hong approached Yin studied—fully obtained his methods.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong studied under Zheng Yin and mastered every technique.

sentences.zh: 後師事南海太守上党鮑玄。

translations.literal: Later served as disciple Nanhai Grand Administrator Shangdang Bao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Nanhai prefect Bao Xuan of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 玄亦內學，逆占將來，見洪深重之，以女妻洪。

translations.literal: Xuan also interior learning—inverse divined future—saw Hong deeply prized him—with daughter wife Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan practiced interior arcana, foresaw Ge Hong's greatness, and married him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 洪傳玄業，兼綜練醫術，凡所著撰，皆精核是非，而才章富贍。

translations.literal: Hong transmitted Xuan enterprise—also synthesized refined medicine arts—whatever composed—all refined examine right wrong—yet talent chapters rich abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong inherited Bao's arts and medicine; every treatise weighed evidence yet read elegantly.

sentences.zh: 太安中，石冰作亂，吳興太守顧秘為義軍都督，與周玘等起兵討之，秘檄洪為將兵都尉，攻冰別率，破之，遷伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Taian within—Shi Bing raised rebellion—Wuxing Grand Administrator Gu Mi became righteous army commander-in-chief—with Zhou Qi etc. raised troops punish—Mi proclamation Hong as command troops commandant—attacked Bing detached force—broke them—transferred Wave-Cutting general.
translations.idiomatic: During Taian Ge Hong joined Gu Mi's loyal army against Shi Bing as commandant, routed a column, and earned promotion to Wave-Pacifying general.

sentences.zh: 冰平，洪不論功賞，徑至洛陽，欲搜求異書以廣其學。

translations.literal: Bing pacified—Hong not discussed merit rewards—straight went Luoyang—wished search unusual books broaden studies.
translations.idiomatic: After victory Ge Hong spurned rewards and hurried to Luoyang hunting rare books.

sentences.zh: 洪見天下已亂，欲避地南土，乃參廣州刺史嵇含軍事。

translations.literal: Hong saw realm already chaotic—wished flee land southern soil—then joined Guangzhou Inspector Xi Han military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chaos Ge Hong joined Guangzhou Inspector Xi Han's staff seeking refuge south.

sentences.zh: 及含遇害，遂停南土多年，征鎮檄命一無所就。

translations.literal: When Han murdered—then halted southern soil many years—campaign defend proclamations orders none accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Han's murder stranded Ge Hong for years; he spurned every summons.

sentences.zh: 後還鄉里，禮辟皆不赴。

translations.literal: Later returned village—ritual summons none attended.
translations.idiomatic: Even recalled home he refused appointments.

sentences.zh: 元帝為丞相，辟為掾。

translations.literal: Yuan Emperor was Chancellor—summoned as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui was chancellor Ge Hong accepted aide duty.

sentences.zh: 以平賊功，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Because pacify bandit merit—gifted rank secondary marquis within passes.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing bandits brought him secondary marquis rank.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，司徒導召補州主簿，轉司徒掾，遷諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Xianhe early—Minister Tutor Dao summoned supplement prefecture chief clerk—transferred Chancellor aide—transferred consultant aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe Wang Dao named him prefect clerk, then chancellor aide, then consultant.

sentences.zh: 干寶深相親友，薦洪才堪國史，選為散騎常侍，領大著作，洪固辭不就。

translations.literal: Gan Bao deeply befriended him—recommended Hong talent fit national history—selected as attendant-in-ordinary—held chief compilation—Hong firmly declined not take.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao befriended Ge Hong and nominated him for court historian; the court named him supernumerary palace attendant and chief editor but Ge Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 以年老，欲練丹以祈遐壽，聞交阯出丹，求為句漏令。

translations.literal: Because aged—wished refine cinnabar pray long life—heard Jiaozhi produced cinnabar—begged become Gou Lou magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Aging, he sought cinnabar for longevity; learning Jiaozhi yielded ore he asked for the magistracy of Gou Lou.

sentences.zh: 帝以洪資高，不許。

translations.literal: Emperor because Hong stature high—not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, deeming him too eminent.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「非欲為榮，以有丹耳。」

translations.literal: Ge Hong said: "I do not wish to do this for glory; it is only because there is cinnabar."
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong said: "I do not wish to do this for glory; it is only because there is cinnabar."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 洪遂將子侄俱行。

translations.literal: Hong then led sons nephews together travel.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong took sons and nephews along.

sentences.zh: 至廣州，刺史鄧岳留不聽去，洪乃止羅浮山煉丹。

translations.literal: Reached Guangzhou—Inspector Deng Yue detained not listen leave—Hong then halted Mount Luofu refine cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Deng Yue detained him; Ge Hong stayed on Mount Luofu to compound elixirs.

sentences.zh: 岳表補東官太守，又辭不就。

translations.literal: Yue memorial supplemented Eastern Office Grand Administrator—again declined not take.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue petitioned him as governor of Eastern Office yet again he declined.

sentences.zh: 岳乃以洪兄子望為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Yue then took Hong elder-brother son Wang as secretary aide.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue instead appointed Ge Hong's nephew Ge Wang secretary.

sentences.zh: 在山積年，優遊閑養，著述不輟。

translations.literal: Within mountains piled years—leisurely roamed idle nourish—writings never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Years on the mountain passed in serene study and ceaseless writing.

sentences.zh: 其自序曰：

translations.literal: His self-preface said:
translations.idiomatic: His own preface reads:

sentences.zh: 洪體乏進趣之才，偶好無為之業。

translations.literal: Hong body lacks advancing zest talent—accidentally loves non-action enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong admits no zeal for climbing office—only love of quiet non-action.

sentences.zh: 假令奮翅則能陵厲玄霄，騁足則能追風躡景，猶欲戢勁翮于於鷦鷃之群，藏逸跡於跛驢之伍，豈況大塊稟我以尋常之短羽，造化假我以至駑之蹇足？

translations.literal: Supposing order flap wings then can scale mystic empyrean—gallop feet then can chase wind tread brilliance—still wishes fold strong pinions amid quail flocks—hide fleet traces among lame donkeys—how mention great clod endows me common short feathers—creation lends me utmost dull lame feet?
translations.idiomatic: Had I wings to pierce the clouds or legs to outrun the gale, I would still hide among quails and limping asses—how much more when heaven gives me ordinary plumage and Creation fits me with stumbling hooves?

sentences.zh: 自卜者審，不能者止，又豈敢力蒼蠅而慕沖天之舉，策跛鱉而追飛兔之軌；

translations.literal: Self diviners examine—cannot ones stop—again how dare force blue-bottle admire sky-soaring deed—spur lame turtle pursue flying hare track;
translations.idiomatic: The wise know their limits; how may a fly aspire aloft or a lame tortoise chase the swiftest hare?

sentences.zh: 飾嫫母之篤陋，求媒陽之美談；

translations.literal: Adorn Mother Mo's deep ugliness—seek match Yang fair praise;
translations.idiomatic: Painting Mother Mo and expecting Yangzhou beauties to praise it—

sentences.zh: 推沙礫之賤質，索千金于和肆哉！

translations.literal: Push sand-gravel's mean substance—seek thousand gold at He market!
translations.idiomatic: —peddling gravel for jade prices in the He market!

sentences.zh: 夫僬僥之步而企及誇父之蹤，近才所以躓礙也；

translations.literal: As Jiaoyao's stride yet stands atop Kuafu's trace—modest talent therefore trips obstructs;
translations.idiomatic: A dwarf aping Kuafu's stride only trips—

sentences.zh: 要離之羸而強赴扛鼎之勢，秦人所以斷筋也。

translations.literal: Yaoli's frail yet strong rush cauldron-lifting force—Qin men therefore sever sinews.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Li lifting tripods broke Qin men's sinews—

sentences.zh: 是以望絕于榮華之途，而志安乎窮圮之域；

translations.literal: Therefore hope cut at glory-flower path—while intent rests in ruined waste realm;
translations.idiomatic: So I abandon ambition on glory's road and rest content in mean lanes;

sentences.zh: 藜藿有八珍之甘，蓬蓽有藻棁之樂也。

translations.literal: Chenopodium has eight-treasure sweetness—hawthorn door has jewelled-rafter joy.
translations.idiomatic: wild greens taste royal fare and hovels bring palace joy.

sentences.zh: 故權貴之家，雖咫尺弗從也；

translations.literal: Therefore power-noble houses—though cubits near not follow;
translations.idiomatic: Mighty houses inches away I shun;

sentences.zh: 知道之士，雖艱遠必造也。

translations.literal: knowing-Dao gentlemen—though hardship far must visit.
translations.idiomatic: men of the Way, however distant, I seek.

sentences.zh: 考覽奇書，既不少矣，率多隱語，難可卒解，自非至精不能尋究，自非篤勤不能悉見也。

translations.literal: Examined perused wonder books—already not few—mostly many hidden language—hard complete sudden solve—if not utmost refined cannot search investigate—if not utmost diligent cannot fully see.
translations.idiomatic: Strange books abound in riddles; without utmost wit and toil none masters them.

sentences.zh: 道士弘博洽聞者寡，而意斷妄說者眾。

translations.literal: Daoist masters vast learned hear few—yet opinion-cut reckless speak many.
translations.idiomatic: Few priests read widely while rash guesswork spreads.

sentences.zh: 至於時有好事者，欲有所修為，倉卒不知所從，而意之所疑又無足諮。

translations.literal: As for times have fond-affair ones—wish have cultivate acts—hasty not know follow what—while intent doubt again none consult.
translations.idiomatic: Would-be adepts rush unsure whom to ask.

sentences.zh: 今為此書，粗舉長生之理。

translations.literal: Now compose this book—roughly raise long-life principle.
translations.idiomatic: This book sketches the principles of longevity.

sentences.zh: 其至妙者不得宣之於翰墨，蓋粗言較略以示一隅，冀悱憤之徒省之可以思過半矣。

translations.literal: Utmost wondrous cannot declare on ink—cover rough words compare outline show one corner—hope troubled hearts save can think half beyond.
translations.idiomatic: The subtlest teachings resist ink; here is a sketch so earnest readers grasp half the lesson.

sentences.zh: 豈謂暗塞必能窮微暢遠乎，聊論其所先覺者耳。

translations.literal: How say blocked obscurity surely exhaust subtle extend far—merely discuss those first awakened ear.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot expose every mystery—only what I already perceive.

sentences.zh: 世儒徒知服膺周孔，莫信神仙之書，不但大而笑之，又將謗毀真正。

translations.literal: Age Ruists vainly know embrace Zhou Kong—none trust transcendents' books—not only great laugh them—again will slander true orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians mock immortal scriptures—some even slander the true teaching.

sentences.zh: 故予所著子言黃白之事，名曰《內篇》，其餘駁難通釋，名曰《外篇》，大凡內外一百一十六篇。

translations.literal: Therefore my composed masters speak yellow-white affairs—named Inner Chapters—remainder refute difficult interpret—named Outer Chapters—generally inner-outer hundred sixteen chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Hence my Inner Chapters on alchemy and Outer Chapters of debate—116 chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 雖不足藏諸名山，且欲緘之金匱，以示識者。

translations.literal: Although not enough hide famous mountains—yet wish seal metal cabinet—show knowing ones.
translations.idiomatic: They may not merit mountain vaults but deserve a golden coffer for discerning eyes.

sentences.zh: 自號抱樸子，因以名書。

translations.literal: Self-styled Master Embracing Simplicity—thereby named book.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Master Embracing Simplicity and titled his book accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其餘所著碑誄詩賦百卷，移檄章表三十卷，神仙、良吏、隱逸、集異等傳各十卷，又抄《五經》、《史》、《漢》、百家之言、方技雜事三百一十卷，《金匱藥方》一百卷，《肘後要急方》四卷。

translations.literal: Remainder composed stele elegies poems fu hundred fascicles—dispatches memorials thirty fascicles—transcendent, good magistrate, recluse, collected marvel biographies each ten fascicles—again excerpt Five Classics, Histories, Han, hundred masters, arts-medley affairs three hundred ten fascicles—Metal Casket Formulas hundred fascicles—Elbow-Lair Emergency Formulas four fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Besides a hundred fascicles of verse and prose, thirty of state papers, and ten each on transcendents, worthy magistrates, recluses, and marvels, he copied 310 fascicles of classics, histories, and technical lore, 100 of Metal Casket Formulas, and 4 of Emergency Formulas from the Elbow Lair.

sentences.zh: 洪博聞深洽，江左絕倫。

translations.literal: Hong vast hear deep unite—Jiang left unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong's erudition was unrivalled south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 著述篇章富於班馬，又精辯玄賾，析理入微。

translations.literal: Writings chapters richer than Ban Ma—again refined debate dark profound—split principle enter subtle.
translations.idiomatic: His corpus outbulked Ban and Sima and dissected arcana to the finest grain.

sentences.zh: 後忽與嶽疏云：「當遠行尋師，克期便發。」

translations.literal: Later he suddenly sent Deng Yue a letter saying: "I must travel far to seek a teacher, and when the appointed time arrives I will set out."
translations.idiomatic: Later he suddenly sent Deng Yue a letter saying: "I must travel far to seek a teacher, and when the appointed time arrives I will set out."

sentences.zh: 嶽得疏，狼狽往別。

translations.literal: Yue obtained memorial—flustered went bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue rushed to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 而洪坐至日中，兀然若睡而卒，嶽至，遂不及見。

translations.literal: Yet Hong sat until noon—silent as sleep then died—Yue arrived—therefore not reach see.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong sat motionless like sleep until noon and died before Deng Yue arrived.

sentences.zh: 時年八十一。

translations.literal: Age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 視其顏色如生，體亦柔軟，舉屍入棺，甚輕，如空衣，世以為屍解得仙雲。

translations.literal: View his complexion like life—body also soft—lift corpse into coffin—very light—as empty clothes—age thought corpse-release attained transcendence cloud.
translations.idiomatic: His colour stayed lifelike, his limbs supple; lifted into the coffin he weighed like empty clothes—people called it corpse liberation and transcendence.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historians' Comment】
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：景純篤志綈緗，洽聞強記，在異書而畢綜，瞻往滯而咸釋；

translations.literal: Historians say: Jingchun devoted archives silk—hears widely remembers strong—in strange books wholly surveyed—gazed past obscurities all released;
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: Guo Pu devoted himself to silk tomes, remembered all he read, mastered exotic texts, and cleared every crux;

sentences.zh: 情源秀逸，思業高奇；

translations.literal: Feeling source elegant drift—thought enterprise lofty strange;
translations.idiomatic: his spirit flowed refined and his ideas soared;

sentences.zh: 襲文雅於西朝，振辭鋒于南夏，為中興才學之宗矣。

translations.literal: Inherited literary elegance Western Jin—vibrated rhetoric blade southern summer—became Restoration talent-learning ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: he inherited Western Jin letters and led southern literature—the patriarch of Restoration letters.

sentences.zh: 夫語怪征神，伎成則賤，前修貽訓，鄙乎茲道。

translations.literal: As for speaking weird summon gods—craft accomplished then base—former worthies left lessons—despise this path.
translations.idiomatic: Tales of spirits win cheap fame once skill turns stale—ancient teachers warned us to scorn such arts.

sentences.zh: 景純之探策定數，考往知來，邁京管於前圖，軼梓窀於遐篆。

translations.literal: Jingchun's exploring stalks fixed fate—examining past know coming—surpasses Jing-Guan former charts—surpasses Zi Shen remote seal-script.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guo Pu's stalk divining surpassed Jing Fang and Guan Lu and outdid astrologers like Zi Shen.

sentences.zh: 而宦微於世，禮薄于時，區區然寄《客傲》以申懷，斯亦伎成之累也。

translations.literal: Yet office minute in age—ritual thin in times—petty lodged Guest Arrogance declare heart—this also craft-accomplished burden.
translations.idiomatic: Office humbled him and ritual slighted him—hence his petty Guest's Pride—a burden of wasted craft.

sentences.zh: 若乃大塊流形，玄天賦命，吉凶修短，定乎自然。

translations.literal: If then great clod flows forms—dark heaven grants fate—auspicious ominous long short—settled in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Great Nature shapes forms and dark Heaven assigns spans—good or ill, long or short rest in what is natural.

sentences.zh: 雖稽象或通，而厭勝難恃，稟之有在，必也無差，自可居常待終，頹心委運，何至銜刀被髮，遑遑于穢向之間哉！

translations.literal: Although investigate images perhaps penetrate—yet apotropaic victory hard rely—endowment has fixed—must without error—self may dwell constant await end—sink heart entrust fate—why arrive bite blade loose hair—frantic amid filthy privies!
translations.idiomatic: Even divination may glimpse fate yet charms cannot be trusted—what is allotted cannot err—one may calmly await destiny—why bite blades and loose hair in frantic sorcery?

sentences.zh: 晚抗忠言，無救王敦之逆；

translations.literal: Late resisted loyal words—none rescue Wang Dun's rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Late loyal words could not stop Wang Dun's revolt;

sentences.zh: 初慚智免，竟斃「山宗」之謀。

translations.literal: First ashamed wise escape—finally killed 'mountain clan' plot.
translations.idiomatic: early wit spared him yet the "mountain clan" prophecy slew him.

sentences.zh: 仲尼所謂攻乎異端，斯害也已，悲夫！

translations.literal: Zhongni so-called attack strange ends—this harm also ended—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius warned against heterodox arts—their harm proves real—alas!

sentences.zh: 稚川束發從師，老而忘倦。

translations.literal: Zhichuan bound hair followed teacher—old yet forgot weary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichuan tied his hair and studied on, tireless in age.

sentences.zh: 紬奇冊府，總百代之遺編；

translations.literal: Draw out wonder archives—gather hundred generations lost compilations;
translations.idiomatic: He threaded marvel vaults and gathered generations of scattered writings;

sentences.zh: 紀化仙都，窮九丹之秘術。

translations.literal: Record transformations immortal capital—exhaust nine-cinnabar secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: he chronicled transcendence and plumbed the ninefold elixir.

sentences.zh: 謝浮榮而捐雜藝，賤尺寶而貴分陰，遊德棲真，超然事外。

translations.literal: Renounced floating glory cast miscellaneous arts—despise foot treasure honour inch shade—wander virtue dwell truth—transcend matters outside.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned vanity and baubles, prized each inch of time, roamed in virtue and lodged in truth beyond worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 全生之道，其最優乎！

translations.literal: Preserve life Way—its most excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Of ways to preserve life his was finest.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：景純通秀，夙振宏材。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Jingchun penetrates elegance—dawn shakes vast talent.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium sings: Jingchun's brilliance shone early and vast.

sentences.zh: 沈研鳥冊，洞曉龜枚。

translations.literal: Deep research bird tablets—thoroughly dawn turtle stalks.
translations.idiomatic: He plumbed omens of birds and turtles.

sentences.zh: 匪甯國釁，坐致身災。

translations.literal: Not only state calamity—sit causes body disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the state no grief yet met personal doom.

sentences.zh: 稚川優洽，貧而樂道。

translations.literal: Zhichuan superior unite—poor yet joyful Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichuan was learned though poor and rejoiced in the Way.

sentences.zh: 載范斯文，永傳洪藻。

translations.literal: Carries norm this pattern—forever transmit Hong brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: His pattern endures and his great letters shine on.
